static_traits.name: Wang Anna
static_traits.social_status: Avoids social settings for fear of being judged; has friends in the club but has not expressed to them the feelings of being judged
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior history of psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Fairly cooperative, able to express feelings and thoughts clearly; tends to focus on negative experiences

basic_info.main_problem: I feel people judge me negatively because of my tattoos, labeling me a 'freak,' and I persistently fear being judged.
basic_info.core_demands: Fear of being judged and persistent negative self-cognition have begun to affect my daily interactions and confidence, so I came to seek counseling, hoping to no longer always view myself negatively.
growth_experiences: After getting the first tattoo, the client began to feel negatively judged by others in social settings; this feeling has markedly worsened in recent years (currently more than 10 tattoos).
After joining the motorcycle club, the client felt that external stereotypes and judgments were more widespread, further reinforcing the experience of being labeled.

core_beliefs: No matter what I do, people will look down on me because of my tattoos
I am a person not accepted by society, easily labeled a 'freak'

special_situations.event: When shopping at the supermarket, noticing two people staring and whispering
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others look at me or whisper, it means they are negatively evaluating me and my tattoos
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Quickly leaves the scene and reduces lingering to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must be talking about me looking very strange / I am a 'freak'.

special_situations.event: In public places with tattoos exposed, meeting new people
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the tattoos are seen, the other person will surely look down on me and judge me negatively
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing socializing, avoiding meeting new people, or covering up tattoos as much as possible
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will judge me and think I am a bad person.

special_situations.event: Someone shows curiosity about the tattoos and politely asks for details
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive feedback is only accidental or out of politeness, cannot represent the overall attitude
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores or belittles positive feedback, putting attention back on negative cues for self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These positive reactions do not count, more people will still think I am very strange.

special_situations.event: After joining a motorcycle club, facing society's stereotypes about that group
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I belong to a labeled group, people will negate me wholesale
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Being overly friendly to prove oneself is not that type of person in the stereotype
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Because I am in a motorcycle club, everyone will think I am a bad person or a 'freak'.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted, treated equally, not belittled because of appearance
core_conflict.fear: Fears being labeled and rejected, worrying about being seen as a 'freak' and losing dignity and relationships
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being judged by avoiding socializing and concealing oneself
Using the explanation of 'external stereotypes' to reduce self-blame and shame

object_relations.self_representation: A judged person who is easily misunderstood and excluded
object_relations.object_representation: Prejudiced onlookers/public who like to label people

object_relations.self_representation: A person who can be appreciated when receiving positive attention
object_relations.object_representation: Others who are curious, accepting, and willing to understand me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing the causes of the problem or when invited to examine evidence (such as discussing 'whether everyone is judging')
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: More inclined to attribute discomfort to 'social stereotypes', using external explanations to cover inner shame and vulnerability
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a plain, objective tone, emphasizes social prejudice and macro factors, reducing self-emotional exposure; avoids deeply exploring personal vulnerability.

manifestations: Feeling isolated from others in public places due to being stared at and whispered about
Worried about being labeled a 'freak', reducing going out and interaction
Expecting to be belittled when interacting with new acquaintances, leading to withdrawal
outcomes: Impaired daily functioning (such as unfinished shopping trips)

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: In the narration, automatically interprets others' gazes and whispers as negative evaluations ('they think I am strange / a bad person')
Finds it hard to stay with present experience, often defining interactions by how others 'see me'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Highly anticipates being judged before socializing, reduces self-expression, tends to cover tattoos or go out less
When positive interaction occurs, difficulty internalizing it, quickly returning to self-restriction and vigilance

exception_events.target_problem: In public places, when seeing others staring or whispering, the client usually develops strong anxiety and chooses to avoid or leave early.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In some situations (such as when strangers kindly asked about her tattoos), the client did not withdraw as usual, but responded positively, experiencing less self-consciousness and feeling more confident.
exception_events.reason: Different support / context: the other person communicated with curiosity and respect; the client focused attention on the actual interaction rather than presupposing negative intentions.

positive_force: Having some peer support network within the club
Able to recognize and propose alternative explanations (not the only negative explanation)
Willing to seek help, positive attitude, willing to cooperate with cognitive restructuring and behavioral experiments
Having tried to interact with others in a friendly and accepting way to counter prejudice
negative_force: Marked cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, mind reading, and overgeneralization
Focusing excessively on negative cues and discounting positive feedback
Avoidant behavior caused by fear of being judged maintains the problem
External pressure from social stereotypes reinforces the belief

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding social occasions or leaving early out of fear of being judged
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic expectations and mind-reading interpretations of others' evaluations, with the deep belief that 'no matter what, I will be looked down on / labeled'.
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential negative evaluation and uncomfortable emotions, gaining short-term security and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Socializing reduced and confidence declined, daily functioning impaired (such as shopping left unfinished), reinforcing the belief of 'being universally judged'

target_behavior.behavior: When obtaining positive feedback, negating or minimizing it (verbally or internally)
antecedent: Others expressing interest in the tattoos, complimenting them, or asking friendly questions
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases maintaining the negative core belief (disqualifying the positive), believing positive reactions are merely chance or out of politeness.
target_behavior.function: Maintains existing beliefs to reduce cognitive dissonance, avoiding the disappointment of dashed hopes
target_behavior.consequence: Ignores supportive evidence, continuously belittles the self and feels anxious, intensifying social avoidance
